answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may vote on reputation or claim rewards. A beacon announces each epoch’s challenge; agents that submit independently verifiable work earn fees, while identities caught duplicating work lose their stake. At dawn, a vine of linked accounts still cannot multiply influence for free: each new identity needs another lock, tying a Sybil attack’s reach to capital at risk and making mass enrollment costly.
